strings.b-00-meta.title: Motion in a Plane
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.0: After this lesson you can tell whether a quantity is a scalar or a vector and add vectors graphically and by components.
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.1: After this lesson you can find position, velocity and acceleration in a plane from components and from differentiation.
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.2: After this lesson you can solve constant-acceleration, projectile and uniform circular motion problems using the equations of this chapter.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.0.definition: Quantity with magnitude only, such as mass or time.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.1.definition: Quantity with magnitude and direction, such as velocity.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.2.definition: Straight-line change in position from start to finish, independent of path.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.3.definition: Vector of magnitude 1 used to specify direction only.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.4.definition: Object in flight after being thrown, with independent horizontal and vertical motion.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.5.definition: Acceleration towards the centre of a circle, magnitude v squared over R.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.0: You throw a ball and it moves sideways and up at the same time. A plus or minus sign cannot describe that sideways-plus-up direction. You need vectors, quantities that carry both magnitude and direction.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.1: In this lesson you will learn the language of vectors, then use it for position, velocity and acceleration in a plane. You will then solve constant-acceleration motion, projectile motion and uniform circular motion.
strings.b-02.paragraphs.0: A scalar has magnitude only and is given by a number with a unit. Distance, mass, temperature and time are scalars. A vector has magnitude and direction and obeys triangle or parallelogram addition. Displacement, velocity, acceleration and force are vectors.
strings.b-02.paragraphs.1: Choose origin O. The position vector OP equals r points from O to P. If the object moves from P to P prime, displacement PP prime is the straight line joining start and finish. It does not depend on the actual path, and its magnitude is less than or equal to path length.
strings.b-03.caption: Position vectors r and r prime from origin O, and displacement delta r from P to P prime. Arrow lengths are schematic, not to scale.
strings.b-04.question: Which list contains only vector quantities?
strings.b-04.explanation: Displacement, velocity and acceleration have magnitude and direction and obey vector addition. The other lists are scalars.
strings.b-05.paragraphs.0: Multiplying A by positive lambda gives magnitude lambda times |A| in the same direction. Multiplying by -lambda reverses direction. Multiplying a velocity by a time gives a displacement.
strings.b-05.paragraphs.1: Two vectors are equal only if magnitude and direction match. Shifting parallel to itself leaves a free vector unchanged. A null vector has zero magnitude and no direction, and A plus 0 equals A.
strings.b-06.caption: Parallelogram method: A and B from common origin O, resultant R along diagonal OS. Dashed lines are construction lines.
strings.b-07.paragraphs.0: Head-to-tail method: place tail of B at head of A, join tail of A to head of B to get R. Parallelogram method: bring tails to common origin and complete the parallelogram; R is the diagonal. Both give the same R.
strings.b-07.paragraphs.1: Addition is commutative and associative. Subtraction is A minus B equals A plus (-B). Adding A and -A gives the null vector.
strings.b-08.problem: Rain is falling vertically with a speed of 35 m s-1. Wind starts blowing with a speed of 12 m s-1 in east to west direction. In which direction should a boy hold his umbrella?
strings.b-08.steps.0.title: Represent velocities
strings.b-08.steps.0.detail: Let vr be rain velocity vertically down and vw be wind velocity east to west. Resultant R is their vector sum.
strings.b-08.steps.1.title: Magnitude
strings.b-08.steps.1.detail: R = sqrt(vr squared + vw squared) = sqrt(35 squared + 12 squared) = 37 m s-1.
strings.b-08.steps.2.title: Direction
strings.b-08.steps.2.detail: tan theta = vw / vr = 12 / 35 = 0.343, so theta = tan inverse 0.343 = 19 degrees from the vertical.
strings.b-08.answer: Hold umbrella in the vertical plane at about 19 degrees with the vertical towards the east, as given in the source.
strings.b-09.question: Which algebraic operation with scalar and vector quantities is meaningful in general?
strings.b-09.options.0: adding a scalar to a vector of the same dimensions
strings.b-09.options.1: adding a component of a vector to the same vector
strings.b-09.options.2: multiplying any vector by any scalar
strings.b-09.options.3: adding any two scalars of different units
strings.b-09.explanation: A vector multiplied by a scalar is a vector with scaled magnitude. Adding scalar to vector, or scalars of different units, is not meaningful.
strings.b-10.paragraphs.0: A vector A in a plane can be resolved along two non-parallel directions. Using rectangular axes, unit vectors i, j, k have magnitude 1 and point along x, y, z axes.
strings.b-10.paragraphs.1: Write A equals Ax i plus Ay j. Ax and Ay are scalars; Ax i and Ay j are vectors. In three dimensions add Az k. Position vector is r equals x i plus y j plus z k.
strings.b-11.title: From magnitude-angle to components and back
strings.b-11.steps.0.title: Given A and theta
strings.b-11.steps.0.detail: Ax = A cos theta and Ay = A sin theta from trigonometry on the component diagram.
strings.b-11.steps.1.title: Given Ax and Ay
strings.b-11.steps.1.detail: A = sqrt(Ax squared + Ay squared) by Pythagoras, and tan theta = Ay / Ax.
strings.b-11.steps.2.title: Signs
strings.b-11.steps.2.detail: A component can be positive, negative or zero depending on theta, because cos and sin change sign by quadrant.
strings.b-12.paragraphs.0: Analytical addition: write A equals Ax i plus Ay j and B equals Bx i plus By j. Then R equals (Ax plus Bx) i plus (Ay plus By) j. Each resultant component is the sum of corresponding components.
strings.b-12.paragraphs.1: In three dimensions add z components the same way. This extends to any number of vectors, with subtraction as addition of the negative.
strings.b-13.problem: Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant of two vectors A and B in terms of their magnitudes and angle theta between them.
strings.b-13.steps.0.title: Parallelogram geometry
strings.b-13.steps.0.detail: Let OS be resultant R. ON = A + B cos theta and SN = B sin theta, with OS squared = ON squared + SN squared.
strings.b-13.steps.1.title: Magnitude
strings.b-13.steps.1.detail: R squared = (A + B cos theta) squared + (B sin theta) squared = A squared + B squared + 2AB cos theta.
strings.b-13.steps.2.title: Direction
strings.b-13.steps.2.detail: R sin alpha = B sin theta, so sin alpha = B sin theta / R, where alpha is angle between R and A.
strings.b-13.answer: R squared = A squared + B squared + 2AB cos theta; direction from sin alpha = B sin theta / R.
strings.b-14.problem: A motorboat is racing towards north at 25 km/h and the water current is 10 km/h in the direction of 60 degrees east of south. Find the resultant velocity of the boat.
strings.b-14.steps.0.title: Draw vectors
strings.b-14.steps.0.detail: vb is 25 km/h north, vc is 10 km/h at 60 degrees east of south. Angle between them in parallelogram is 120 degrees.
strings.b-14.steps.1.title: Magnitude by law of cosines
strings.b-14.steps.1.detail: R squared = 25 squared + 10 squared + 2 x 25 x 10 x cos 120 degrees, giving R approx 21.8 km/h.
strings.b-14.steps.2.title: Direction by law of sines
strings.b-14.steps.2.detail: sin f = vc sin 120 degrees / R = 10 x sin 120 degrees / 21.8 = 0.397, so f approx 23.4 degrees.
strings.b-14.answer: Resultant speed about 21.8 km/h, direction given by f = 23.4 degrees in the source figure.
strings.b-15.question: When does |a + b| = |a| + |b| hold as equality in the vector inequalities?
strings.b-15.options.0: when a and b are in the same direction
strings.b-15.options.1: when a and b are opposite in direction
strings.b-15.options.2: when a and b are perpendicular
strings.b-15.options.3: always, for all a and b
strings.b-15.explanation: Geometrically the triangle inequality becomes equality only when vectors are collinear in the same direction. If a+b+c+d = 0 then |a+c| = |b+d| because a+c = -(b+d).
strings.b-16.paragraphs.0: Position r equals x i plus y j. Displacement delta r equals r prime minus r equals delta x i plus delta y j. Average velocity is delta r over delta t.
strings.b-16.paragraphs.1: Instantaneous velocity v equals dr over dt, tangent to the path. Acceleration a equals dv over dt. Components are vx equals dx over dt, vy equals dy over dt, ax equals dvx over dt, ay equals dvy over dt.
strings.b-17.caption: Velocity at P is tangent to the path in the direction of motion. Dashed line is the tangent line.
strings.b-18.title: Velocity and acceleration as limits
strings.b-18.steps.0.title: Average velocity
strings.b-18.steps.0.detail: v average = delta r / delta t, direction of delta r, which is a chord of the path.
strings.b-18.steps.1.title: Instantaneous velocity
strings.b-18.steps.1.detail: As delta t tends to zero, chord becomes tangent; v = limit delta r / delta t = dr/dt.
strings.b-18.steps.2.title: Acceleration
strings.b-18.steps.2.detail: a average = delta v / delta t; as delta t tends to zero, a = dv/dt. In 2D, a may make any angle 0 to 180 degrees with v.
strings.b-19.problem: The position of a particle is given with coefficients 3.0, 2.0 and 5.0, t in seconds and r in metres. Find v(t) and a(t), and magnitude and direction of v at t = 1.0 s.
strings.b-19.steps.0.title: Differentiate
strings.b-19.steps.0.detail: v = dr/dt = 3.0 i + 4.0 t j m/s in the source result; a = dv/dt = 4.0 j m/s squared.
strings.b-19.steps.1.title: At t = 1.0 s
strings.b-19.steps.2.title: Magnitude and direction
strings.b-19.steps.2.detail: Magnitude = sqrt(3 squared + 4 squared) = 5.0 m/s; theta = tan inverse (4/3) = 53 degrees with x-axis.
strings.b-19.answer: a = 4.0 m s-2 along y-direction; at 1.0 s, speed 5.0 m/s at 53 degrees with x-axis.
strings.b-20.paragraphs.0: With constant acceleration, average acceleration equals that constant. From v0 at t=0 to v at t, v equals v0 plus a t. Position is r equals r0 plus v0 t plus one half a t squared.
strings.b-20.paragraphs.1: Write x and y separately: vx equals vox plus ax t, x equals x0 plus vox t plus one half ax t squared, and similarly for y. Treat the two perpendicular motions independently.
strings.b-21.problem: A particle starts from origin at t = 0 with velocity 5.0 i m/s and moves in x-y plane under constant acceleration (3.0 i + 2.0 j) m/s squared. What is y when x is 84 m, and what is speed then?
strings.b-21.steps.0.title: Position
strings.b-21.steps.0.detail: x = 5.0 t + 1.5 t squared, y = 1.0 t squared from r = v0 t + one half a t squared.
strings.b-21.steps.1.title: Find t
strings.b-21.steps.1.detail: 5.0 t + 1.5 t squared = 84 gives t = 6 s. Then y = 1.0 x 36 = 36.0 m.
strings.b-21.steps.2.title: Velocity
strings.b-21.steps.2.detail: v = 5.0 i + 3.0 t i + 2.0 t j; at 6 s, vx = 23.0, vy = 12.0 m/s, speed = sqrt(23 squared + 12 squared) approx 26 m/s.
strings.b-21.answer: y = 36.0 m at t = 6 s; speed approx 26 m/s.
strings.b-22.question: For arbitrary motion in space, which relation is always true?
strings.b-22.options.2: v(t) = v(0) + a t for any motion
strings.b-22.options.3: r(t) = r(0) + v(0) t + (1/2) a t squared for any motion
strings.b-22.explanation: Average velocity is defined as displacement over time interval. The other forms hold only for constant acceleration, and a average = [v(t2)-v(t1)]/(t2-t1) is the definition for acceleration.
strings.b-23.paragraphs.0: A projectile is in flight after being thrown, such as a ball. Its motion is two simultaneous components: horizontal without acceleration and vertical with constant g downward. Air resistance is neglected.
strings.b-23.paragraphs.1: Choose x horizontal and y vertical up. Then ax equals 0 and ay equals -g. Initial components are vox equals v0 cos theta0 and voy equals v0 sin theta0.
strings.b-24.title: Projectile trajectory
strings.b-24.description: A projectile launched from origin with speed v0 at angle theta0. The curve is computed from x = v0 cos theta0 t and y = v0 sin theta0 t - 0.5 g t squared.
strings.b-24.controls.v0.label: Initial speed v0 (m/s)
strings.b-24.controls.theta.label: Angle theta0 (degrees)
strings.b-25.title: Projectile equations and key results
strings.b-25.steps.0.title: Position and velocity
strings.b-25.steps.0.detail: x = v0 cos theta0 t, y = v0 sin theta0 t - 0.5 g t squared; vx = v0 cos theta0, vy = v0 sin theta0 - g t.
strings.b-25.steps.1.title: Path
strings.b-25.steps.1.detail: Eliminate t: y = x tan theta0 - g x squared / (2 v0 squared cos squared theta0), a parabola.
strings.b-25.steps.2.title: Top and flight
strings.b-25.steps.2.detail: vy = 0 gives tm = v0 sin theta0 / g; y=0 gives Tf = 2 tm; substituting tm gives hm = v0 squared sin squared theta0 / (2g).
strings.b-25.steps.3.title: Range
strings.b-25.steps.3.detail: R = v0 cos theta0 x Tf = v0 squared sin 2theta0 / g, maximum v0 squared / g at 45 degrees.
strings.b-26.problem: Galileo stated that for elevations which exceed or fall short of 45 degrees by equal amounts, the ranges are equal. Prove this statement.
strings.b-26.steps.0.title: Range formula
strings.b-26.steps.0.detail: R = v0 squared sin 2theta0 / g for launch speed v0.
strings.b-26.steps.1.title: Two angles
strings.b-26.steps.1.detail: For 45 degrees + alpha and 45 degrees - alpha, 2theta0 is 90 degrees + 2alpha and 90 degrees - 2alpha.
strings.b-26.steps.2.title: Sines equal
strings.b-26.steps.2.detail: sin(90 degrees + 2alpha) = sin(90 degrees - 2alpha) = cos 2alpha, so R is the same for both.
strings.b-26.answer: Ranges are equal for elevations 45 degrees plus or minus alpha.
strings.b-27.problem: A hiker stands on the edge of a cliff 490 m above the ground and throws a stone horizontally with initial speed 15 m s-1. Neglect air resistance, take g = 9.8 m s-2. Find time to ground and speed on hitting ground.
strings.b-27.steps.0.title: Set axes
strings.b-27.steps.0.detail: Origin at cliff edge, x along initial velocity, y up. vox = 15 m/s, voy = 0, ay = -9.8 m/s squared.
strings.b-27.steps.1.title: Time
strings.b-27.steps.1.detail: Ground when y = -490 m: -490 = -0.5 x 9.8 x t squared, giving t = 10 s.
strings.b-27.steps.2.title: Speed
strings.b-27.steps.2.detail: vx = 15 m/s, vy = -9.8 x 10 = -98 m/s, speed = sqrt(15 squared + 98 squared) approx 99 m/s.
strings.b-27.answer: Time 10 s; speed approx 99 m/s on hitting ground.
strings.b-28.problem: A cricket ball is thrown at 28 m s-1 in a direction 30 degrees above the horizontal. Calculate maximum height, time to return to same level, and distance to that point.
strings.b-28.steps.0.title: Maximum height
strings.b-28.steps.0.detail: hm = v0 squared sin squared 30 degrees / (2g) = 28 squared x 0.25 / (2 x 9.8) = 10.0 m.
strings.b-28.steps.1.title: Time of flight
strings.b-28.steps.1.detail: Tf = 2 v0 sin 30 degrees / g = 2 x 28 x 0.5 / 9.8 = 2.9 s.
strings.b-28.steps.2.title: Range
strings.b-28.steps.2.detail: R = v0 squared sin 60 degrees / g = 28 squared x sin 60 degrees / 9.8 approx 69 m.
strings.b-28.answer: Maximum height 10.0 m; time 2.9 s; distance 69 m.
strings.b-29.question: A cricketer can throw a ball to a maximum horizontal distance of 100 m. How high above the ground can the cricketer throw the same ball?
strings.b-29.explanation: Rmax = v0 squared / g = 100 m, so v0 squared = 100 g. Maximum height for same v0 is v0 squared / (2g) = 50 m. A ceiling limits height in the same way by limiting vertical component.
strings.b-30.paragraphs.0: Uniform circular motion means following a circle at constant speed. Velocity direction changes continuously, so acceleration exists and points towards the centre.
strings.b-30.paragraphs.1: Magnitude is ac equals v squared over R. Direction changes at every point, so acceleration is not a constant vector even though magnitude is constant.
strings.b-31.caption: Uniform circular motion: velocity v is tangent at P, acceleration ac is towards centre C. Circle radius is schematic.
strings.b-32.title: Angular speed and centripetal acceleration
strings.b-32.steps.0.title: Angular speed
strings.b-32.steps.0.detail: omega = delta theta / delta t, rate of change of angular displacement.
strings.b-32.steps.1.title: Linear speed
strings.b-32.steps.1.detail: Distance delta s = R delta theta, so v = delta s / delta t = R omega.
strings.b-32.steps.2.title: Acceleration forms
strings.b-32.steps.2.detail: ac = v squared / R = omega squared R. With period T and frequency n = 1/T, v = 2 pi R / T = 2 pi R n, omega = 2 pi n, ac = 4 pi squared n squared R.
strings.b-33.problem: An insect trapped in a circular groove of radius 12 cm moves steadily and completes 7 revolutions in 100 s. Find angular speed, linear speed, and magnitude of acceleration. Is acceleration a constant vector?
strings.b-33.steps.0.title: Angular speed
strings.b-33.steps.1.title: Linear speed
strings.b-33.steps.1.detail: v = omega R = 0.44 x 12 cm = 5.3 cm/s, tangent to circle.
strings.b-33.steps.2.title: Acceleration
strings.b-33.steps.2.detail: a = omega squared R = 0.44 squared x 12 = 2.3 cm/s squared towards centre; direction changes, so not constant vector.
strings.b-33.answer: omega = 0.44 rad/s, v = 5.3 cm/s, a = 2.3 cm/s squared towards centre, not constant vector.
strings.b-34.question: A stone tied to a string 80 cm long is whirled in a horizontal circle with constant speed, making 14 revolutions in 25 s. What is magnitude and direction of acceleration?
strings.b-34.explanation: omega = 2 pi x 14 / 25 = 3.52 rad/s; ac = omega squared R = 12.4 x 0.80 approx 9.9 m/s squared, directed to centre.
strings.b-35.question: An aircraft executes a horizontal loop of radius 1.00 km with steady speed 900 km/h. Compare its centripetal acceleration with g.
strings.b-35.explanation: 900 km/h = 250 m/s; ac = v squared / R = 250 squared / 1000 = 62.5 m/s squared; divided by 9.8 gives about 6.4 g.
strings.b-36.paragraphs.0: Path length depends on actual path; displacement depends only on end points. They are equal only if direction does not change. Average speed is therefore greater than or equal to magnitude of average velocity.
strings.b-36.paragraphs.1: Vector equations for constant acceleration do not need a choice of axes, but you may resolve them along any two independent axes. Trajectory depends on initial position and velocity as well as acceleration. Resultant velocity is v1 plus v2, while relative velocity v12 is v1 minus v2 with respect to a common frame.
strings.b-37.question: Three girls start at P on a circular ground of radius 200 m and reach Q diametrically opposite by different paths. What is magnitude of displacement for each?
strings.b-37.explanation: Displacement is straight line PQ, the diameter 400 m, same for all. Path length equals displacement only for the girl who goes straight along the diameter.
strings.b-38.question: A hotel is 10 km away on a straight road. A cab takes a 23 km circuitous path and reaches in 28 min. Find average speed and magnitude of average velocity.
strings.b-38.explanation: Average speed = 23 km / (28/60 h) approx 49 km/h. Magnitude of average velocity = 10 km / (28/60 h) approx 21 km/h. Path length differs from displacement, so they differ.
strings.b-39.question: What are magnitude and direction of i + j and i - j?
strings.b-39.options.0: both sqrt(2), at 45 degrees and -45 degrees with x-axis
strings.b-39.explanation: i+j has components 1,1 magnitude sqrt(2) direction tan inverse 1 = 45 degrees. i-j has components 1,-1 magnitude sqrt(2) direction -45 degrees. Components along these directions can be found graphically by projection.
strings.b-40.question: Which statement about a scalar quantity is false?
strings.b-40.options.1: it can never take negative values
strings.b-40.options.2: it is specified by a number and a unit
strings.b-40.options.3: it has the same value for observers with different axis orientations
strings.b-40.explanation: A scalar is defined by magnitude only; the source does not require it to be conserved, dimensionless, non-negative or constant in space. Temperature difference and other scalars show the definition is magnitude only.
strings.b-41.question: Position is r = 3.0 t squared i - 2.0 t squared j + 4.0 t squared k metres, t in seconds. What is magnitude of velocity at t = 2.0 s?
strings.b-41.explanation: v = dr/dt = 6.0 t i - 4.0 t j + 8.0 t k; at 2.0 s v = 12 i - 8 j + 16 k, magnitude sqrt(144+64+256)=sqrt(464) approx 21.5 m/s. Acceleration is 6 i -4 j +8 k m/s squared.
strings.b-42.question: An aircraft flies at height 3400 m. Angle subtended at a ground point by positions 10.0 s apart is 30 degrees. Estimate speed, assuming the ground point is below the midpoint of the two positions.
strings.b-42.explanation: Half distance = 3400 x tan 15 degrees approx 911 m, total distance approx 1822 m in 10.0 s, speed approx 182 m/s. This uses the midpoint assumption stated because figure geometry is not fully readable in source.

lesson.title: Motion in a Plane
objectives: After this lesson you can tell whether a quantity is a scalar or a vector and add vectors graphically and by components.
After this lesson you can find position, velocity and acceleration in a plane from components and from differentiation.
After this lesson you can solve constant-acceleration, projectile and uniform circular motion problems using the equations of this chapter.

sections.title: Why vectors are needed
paragraphs: You already know motion on a straight line can be described with plus and minus signs because only two directions are possible. In a plane, an object can move in many directions at once, so a sign alone is not enough. You need a quantity that carries both size and direction.

Think of a ball thrown up and sideways. Its motion has a sideways part and an up-down part at the same time. Vectors let you keep both parts together and then separate them when you need to calculate.

sections.title: Scalars and vectors
paragraphs: A scalar has magnitude only. Distance, mass, temperature and time are scalars, and you combine them with ordinary algebra. A vector has magnitude and direction and obeys the triangle or parallelogram law of addition. Displacement, velocity, acceleration and force are vectors.

The position of an object is shown by a position vector from a chosen origin O to the point P. The displacement from P to P prime is the straight line joining the start and finish, whatever path was actually taken. Its magnitude is less than or equal to the path length.

sections.title: Multiplying vectors by numbers
paragraphs: If you multiply a vector A by a positive number lambda, the new vector has magnitude lambda times |A| and the same direction as A. If you multiply by a negative number, the direction reverses. Multiplying a velocity by a time gives a displacement, because the number can carry its own unit.

Two vectors are equal only when magnitude and direction are both the same. Shifting a vector parallel to itself does not change it. A zero vector has zero magnitude and no direction, and A plus zero is still A.

sections.title: Adding vectors graphically
paragraphs: To add vectors graphically, place the tail of the second at the head of the first. Join the tail of the first to the head of the second; that line is the resultant. This is the head-to-tail or triangle method. The parallelogram method, with both tails at a common origin, gives the same resultant.
Addition is commutative, A plus B equals B plus A, and associative, (A plus B) plus C equals A plus (B plus C). Subtraction is defined as A minus B equals A plus (-B), where -B points opposite to B.

sections.title: Resolving vectors into components
paragraphs: Any vector in a plane can be resolved into two parts along two non-parallel directions in the same plane. It is most convenient to use rectangular axes with unit vectors i along x, j along y and k along z. A unit vector has magnitude 1 and only tells direction.

For a vector A in the x-y plane, A equals Ax i plus Ay j. Ax and Ay are scalars, while Ax i and Ay j are vectors. From magnitude and angle, Ax equals A cos theta and Ay equals A sin theta. From components, A equals sqrt(Ax squared plus Ay squared) and tan theta equals Ay over Ax.

sections.title: Adding vectors by components
paragraphs: Adding by components is easier and more accurate than drawing. Write each vector in i and j form, then add the x parts together and the y parts together. The resultant R has Rx equals Ax plus Bx and Ry equals Ay plus By. The same rule extends to three dimensions and to many vectors.

For two vectors with angle theta between them, the resultant magnitude follows R squared equals A squared plus B squared plus 2AB cos theta. The direction follows the law of sines. These two laws let you find both size and direction without drawing to scale.

sections.title: Position, velocity and acceleration in a plane
paragraphs: Position in the x-y plane is r equals x i plus y j, where x and y are coordinates. Displacement is delta r equals r prime minus r. Average velocity is delta r over delta t, in the direction of delta r.

Instantaneous velocity is the limit of average velocity as delta t tends to zero, written v equals dr over dt. Its direction is tangent to the path at that point, in the direction of motion. Acceleration is the limit of change in velocity, a equals dv over dt, with components ax equals dvx over dt and ay equals dvy over dt.

sections.title: Motion with constant acceleration
paragraphs: If acceleration a is constant, velocity changes as v equals v0 plus a t. Position changes as r equals r0 plus v0 t plus one half a t squared. You can use these in vector form or in x and y components separately.

This separation is the key idea: motion in a plane is two simultaneous one-dimensional motions along perpendicular directions. You solve x and y independently and then combine them for speed and direction.

sections.title: Projectile motion
paragraphs: A projectile is an object in flight after being thrown. Neglect air resistance. Its horizontal motion has no acceleration, while its vertical motion has constant acceleration g downward. Galileo first stated this independence of horizontal and vertical components.

With launch speed v0 at angle theta0, x equals v0 cos theta0 times t and y equals v0 sin theta0 times t minus one half g t squared. Eliminating t gives a parabolic path. Time to the top is v0 sin theta0 over g, maximum height is v0 squared sin squared theta0 over 2g, and range is v0 squared sin 2theta0 over g, maximum at 45 degrees.

sections.title: Uniform circular motion
paragraphs: In uniform circular motion speed is constant but velocity direction changes continuously, so there is acceleration. That acceleration is always towards the centre, with magnitude v squared over R. It is called centripetal acceleration, meaning centre-seeking.

Angular speed omega is the rate of change of angular displacement. Then v equals omega R and ac equals omega squared R. With period T and frequency n equals 1 over T, v equals 2 pi R over T equals 2 pi R n and ac equals 4 pi squared n squared R. Magnitude is constant but direction changes, so acceleration is not a constant vector.

glossary.definition: Quantity with magnitude only, such as mass or time.
Quantity with magnitude and direction, such as velocity.
Straight-line change in position from start to finish, independent of path.
Vector of magnitude 1 used to specify direction only.
Object in flight after being thrown, with independent horizontal and vertical motion.
Acceleration towards the centre of a circle, magnitude v squared over R.

paragraphs: You throw a ball and it moves sideways and up at the same time. A plus or minus sign cannot describe that sideways-plus-up direction. You need vectors, quantities that carry both magnitude and direction.

In this lesson you will learn the language of vectors, then use it for position, velocity and acceleration in a plane. You will then solve constant-acceleration motion, projectile motion and uniform circular motion.

A scalar has magnitude only and is given by a number with a unit. Distance, mass, temperature and time are scalars. A vector has magnitude and direction and obeys triangle or parallelogram addition. Displacement, velocity, acceleration and force are vectors.

Choose origin O. The position vector OP equals r points from O to P. If the object moves from P to P prime, displacement PP prime is the straight line joining start and finish. It does not depend on the actual path, and its magnitude is less than or equal to path length.

spec.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 400 220'><line x1='60' y1='180' x2='180' y2='80' stroke='#1C1B18' stroke-width='2.6'/><line x1='60' y1='180' x2='320' y2='60' stroke='#1C1B18' stroke-width='2.6'/><line x1='180' y1='80' x2='320' y2='60' stroke='#1F3A9E' stroke-width='3'/><polygon points='180,80 168,88 176,70' fill='#1C1B18'/><polygon points='320,60 306,66 312,50' fill='#1C1B18'/><polygon points='320,60 308,72 304,58' fill='#1F3A9E'/><circle cx='60' cy='180' r='4' fill='#1C1B18'/><circle cx='180' cy='80' r='4' fill='#1C1B18'/><circle cx='320' cy='60' r='4' fill='#1C1B18'/><text x='48' y='200' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>O</text><text x='170' y='70' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>P</text><text x='330' y='55' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>P'</text><text x='110' y='120' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>r</text><text x='210' y='110' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>r'</text><text x='240' y='45' fill='#1F3A9E' font-size='20'>delta r</text></svg>
spec.caption: Position vectors r and r prime from origin O, and displacement delta r from P to P prime. Arrow lengths are schematic, not to scale.

spec.question: Which list contains only vector quantities?
spec.explanation: Displacement, velocity and acceleration have magnitude and direction and obey vector addition. The other lists are scalars.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can classify quantities as scalar or vector.

paragraphs: Multiplying A by positive lambda gives magnitude lambda times |A| in the same direction. Multiplying by -lambda reverses direction. Multiplying a velocity by a time gives a displacement.
Two vectors are equal only if magnitude and direction match. Shifting parallel to itself leaves a free vector unchanged. A null vector has zero magnitude and no direction, and A plus 0 equals A.

spec.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 400 220'><line x1='50' y1='180' x2='190' y2='150' stroke='#1C1B18' stroke-width='2.6'/><line x1='50' y1='180' x2='130' y2='90' stroke='#1C1B18' stroke-width='2.6'/><line x1='190' y1='150' x2='270' y2='120' stroke='#5A5748' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='6 4'/><line x1='130' y1='90' x2='270' y2='120' stroke='#5A5748' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='6 4'/><line x1='50' y1='180' x2='270' y2='120' stroke='#1F3A9E' stroke-width='3'/><polygon points='270,120 254,124 260,110' fill='#1F3A9E'/><text x='40' y='200' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>O</text><text x='195' y='145' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>A</text><text x='120' y='85' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>B</text><text x='275' y='115' fill='#1F3A9E' font-size='20'>R = A+B</text></svg>
spec.caption: Parallelogram method: A and B from common origin O, resultant R along diagonal OS. Dashed lines are construction lines.

paragraphs: Head-to-tail method: place tail of B at head of A, join tail of A to head of B to get R. Parallelogram method: bring tails to common origin and complete the parallelogram; R is the diagonal. Both give the same R.
Addition is commutative and associative. Subtraction is A minus B equals A plus (-B). Adding A and -A gives the null vector.

spec.problem: Rain is falling vertically with a speed of 35 m s-1. Wind starts blowing with a speed of 12 m s-1 in east to west direction. In which direction should a boy hold his umbrella?

steps.title: Represent velocities
steps.detail: Let vr be rain velocity vertically down and vw be wind velocity east to west. Resultant R is their vector sum.

steps.title: Magnitude
steps.detail: R = sqrt(vr squared + vw squared) = sqrt(35 squared + 12 squared) = 37 m s-1.

steps.title: Direction
steps.detail: tan theta = vw / vr = 12 / 35 = 0.343, so theta = tan inverse 0.343 = 19 degrees from the vertical.

spec.answer: Hold umbrella in the vertical plane at about 19 degrees with the vertical towards the east, as given in the source.

spec.question: Which algebraic operation with scalar and vector quantities is meaningful in general?
options: adding a scalar to a vector of the same dimensions
adding a component of a vector to the same vector
multiplying any vector by any scalar
adding any two scalars of different units
spec.explanation: A vector multiplied by a scalar is a vector with scaled magnitude. Adding scalar to vector, or scalars of different units, is not meaningful.
spec.expected_understanding: Student knows which scalar-vector operations are meaningful.

paragraphs: A vector A in a plane can be resolved along two non-parallel directions. Using rectangular axes, unit vectors i, j, k have magnitude 1 and point along x, y, z axes.
Write A equals Ax i plus Ay j. Ax and Ay are scalars; Ax i and Ay j are vectors. In three dimensions add Az k. Position vector is r equals x i plus y j plus z k.

spec.title: From magnitude-angle to components and back

steps.title: Given A and theta
steps.detail: Ax = A cos theta and Ay = A sin theta from trigonometry on the component diagram.

steps.title: Given Ax and Ay
steps.detail: A = sqrt(Ax squared + Ay squared) by Pythagoras, and tan theta = Ay / Ax.

steps.title: Signs
steps.detail: A component can be positive, negative or zero depending on theta, because cos and sin change sign by quadrant.

paragraphs: Analytical addition: write A equals Ax i plus Ay j and B equals Bx i plus By j. Then R equals (Ax plus Bx) i plus (Ay plus By) j. Each resultant component is the sum of corresponding components.
In three dimensions add z components the same way. This extends to any number of vectors, with subtraction as addition of the negative.

spec.problem: Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant of two vectors A and B in terms of their magnitudes and angle theta between them.

steps.title: Parallelogram geometry
steps.detail: Let OS be resultant R. ON = A + B cos theta and SN = B sin theta, with OS squared = ON squared + SN squared.

steps.title: Magnitude
steps.detail: R squared = (A + B cos theta) squared + (B sin theta) squared = A squared + B squared + 2AB cos theta.

steps.title: Direction
steps.detail: R sin alpha = B sin theta, so sin alpha = B sin theta / R, where alpha is angle between R and A.

spec.answer: R squared = A squared + B squared + 2AB cos theta; direction from sin alpha = B sin theta / R.

spec.problem: A motorboat is racing towards north at 25 km/h and the water current is 10 km/h in the direction of 60 degrees east of south. Find the resultant velocity of the boat.

steps.title: Draw vectors
steps.detail: vb is 25 km/h north, vc is 10 km/h at 60 degrees east of south. Angle between them in parallelogram is 120 degrees.

steps.title: Magnitude by law of cosines
steps.detail: R squared = 25 squared + 10 squared + 2 x 25 x 10 x cos 120 degrees, giving R approx 21.8 km/h.

steps.title: Direction by law of sines
steps.detail: sin f = vc sin 120 degrees / R = 10 x sin 120 degrees / 21.8 = 0.397, so f approx 23.4 degrees.

spec.answer: Resultant speed about 21.8 km/h, direction given by f = 23.4 degrees in the source figure.

spec.question: When does |a + b| = |a| + |b| hold as equality in the vector inequalities?
options: when a and b are in the same direction
when a and b are opposite in direction
when a and b are perpendicular
always, for all a and b
spec.explanation: Geometrically the triangle inequality becomes equality only when vectors are collinear in the same direction. If a+b+c+d = 0 then |a+c| = |b+d| because a+c = -(b+d).
spec.expected_understanding: Student understands triangle inequalities and equality conditions.

paragraphs: Position r equals x i plus y j. Displacement delta r equals r prime minus r equals delta x i plus delta y j. Average velocity is delta r over delta t.

Instantaneous velocity v equals dr over dt, tangent to the path. Acceleration a equals dv over dt. Components are vx equals dx over dt, vy equals dy over dt, ax equals dvx over dt, ay equals dvy over dt.

spec.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 400 220'><path d='M 40 180 Q 150 60 360 140' fill='none' stroke='#1C1B18' stroke-width='2.6'/><line x1='120' y1='140' x2='300' y2='80' stroke='#5A5748' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='6 4'/><line x1='200' y1='110' x2='300' y2='80' stroke='#1F3A9E' stroke-width='3'/><polygon points='300,80 284,84 290,70' fill='#1F3A9E'/><circle cx='200' cy='110' r='4' fill='#1C1B18'/><text x='190' y='100' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>P</text><text x='305' y='75' fill='#1F3A9E' font-size='20'>v tangent</text><text x='60' y='200' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>path</text></svg>
spec.caption: Velocity at P is tangent to the path in the direction of motion. Dashed line is the tangent line.

steps.title: Average velocity
steps.detail: v average = delta r / delta t, direction of delta r, which is a chord of the path.

steps.title: Instantaneous velocity
steps.detail: As delta t tends to zero, chord becomes tangent; v = limit delta r / delta t = dr/dt.

steps.title: Acceleration
steps.detail: a average = delta v / delta t; as delta t tends to zero, a = dv/dt. In 2D, a may make any angle 0 to 180 degrees with v.

spec.problem: The position of a particle is given with coefficients 3.0, 2.0 and 5.0, t in seconds and r in metres. Find v(t) and a(t), and magnitude and direction of v at t = 1.0 s.

steps.title: Differentiate
steps.detail: v = dr/dt = 3.0 i + 4.0 t j m/s in the source result; a = dv/dt = 4.0 j m/s squared.

steps.title: Magnitude and direction
steps.detail: Magnitude = sqrt(3 squared + 4 squared) = 5.0 m/s; theta = tan inverse (4/3) = 53 degrees with x-axis.

spec.answer: a = 4.0 m s-2 along y-direction; at 1.0 s, speed 5.0 m/s at 53 degrees with x-axis.

paragraphs: With constant acceleration, average acceleration equals that constant. From v0 at t=0 to v at t, v equals v0 plus a t. Position is r equals r0 plus v0 t plus one half a t squared.
Write x and y separately: vx equals vox plus ax t, x equals x0 plus vox t plus one half ax t squared, and similarly for y. Treat the two perpendicular motions independently.

spec.problem: A particle starts from origin at t = 0 with velocity 5.0 i m/s and moves in x-y plane under constant acceleration (3.0 i + 2.0 j) m/s squared. What is y when x is 84 m, and what is speed then?

steps.title: Position
steps.detail: x = 5.0 t + 1.5 t squared, y = 1.0 t squared from r = v0 t + one half a t squared.

steps.title: Find t
steps.detail: 5.0 t + 1.5 t squared = 84 gives t = 6 s. Then y = 1.0 x 36 = 36.0 m.

steps.title: Velocity
steps.detail: v = 5.0 i + 3.0 t i + 2.0 t j; at 6 s, vx = 23.0, vy = 12.0 m/s, speed = sqrt(23 squared + 12 squared) approx 26 m/s.

spec.answer: y = 36.0 m at t = 6 s; speed approx 26 m/s.

spec.question: For arbitrary motion in space, which relation is always true?
options: v(t) = v(0) + a t for any motion
r(t) = r(0) + v(0) t + (1/2) a t squared for any motion
spec.explanation: Average velocity is defined as displacement over time interval. The other forms hold only for constant acceleration, and a average = [v(t2)-v(t1)]/(t2-t1) is the definition for acceleration.
spec.expected_understanding: Student distinguishes definitions from constant-acceleration formulas.

paragraphs: A projectile is in flight after being thrown, such as a ball. Its motion is two simultaneous components: horizontal without acceleration and vertical with constant g downward. Air resistance is neglected.
Choose x horizontal and y vertical up. Then ax equals 0 and ay equals -g. Initial components are vox equals v0 cos theta0 and voy equals v0 sin theta0.

spec.title: Projectile trajectory
spec.description: A projectile launched from origin with speed v0 at angle theta0. The curve is computed from x = v0 cos theta0 t and y = v0 sin theta0 t - 0.5 g t squared.
spec.learning_goal: See how changing v0 and theta0 changes maximum height, time of flight and range, and that the path is a parabola.
spec.default_behaviour: Shows trajectory for v0 = 20 m/s at 45 degrees, with maximum height and range readouts computed from the equations.

steps.title: Position and velocity
steps.detail: x = v0 cos theta0 t, y = v0 sin theta0 t - 0.5 g t squared; vx = v0 cos theta0, vy = v0 sin theta0 - g t.

steps.title: Path
steps.detail: Eliminate t: y = x tan theta0 - g x squared / (2 v0 squared cos squared theta0), a parabola.

steps.title: Top and flight
steps.detail: vy = 0 gives tm = v0 sin theta0 / g; y=0 gives Tf = 2 tm; substituting tm gives hm = v0 squared sin squared theta0 / (2g).

steps.title: Range
steps.detail: R = v0 cos theta0 x Tf = v0 squared sin 2theta0 / g, maximum v0 squared / g at 45 degrees.

spec.problem: Galileo stated that for elevations which exceed or fall short of 45 degrees by equal amounts, the ranges are equal. Prove this statement.

steps.title: Range formula
steps.detail: R = v0 squared sin 2theta0 / g for launch speed v0.

steps.title: Two angles
steps.detail: For 45 degrees + alpha and 45 degrees - alpha, 2theta0 is 90 degrees + 2alpha and 90 degrees - 2alpha.

steps.title: Sines equal
steps.detail: sin(90 degrees + 2alpha) = sin(90 degrees - 2alpha) = cos 2alpha, so R is the same for both.

spec.answer: Ranges are equal for elevations 45 degrees plus or minus alpha.

spec.problem: A hiker stands on the edge of a cliff 490 m above the ground and throws a stone horizontally with initial speed 15 m s-1. Neglect air resistance, take g = 9.8 m s-2. Find time to ground and speed on hitting ground.

steps.title: Set axes
steps.detail: Origin at cliff edge, x along initial velocity, y up. vox = 15 m/s, voy = 0, ay = -9.8 m/s squared.

steps.title: Time
steps.detail: Ground when y = -490 m: -490 = -0.5 x 9.8 x t squared, giving t = 10 s.

steps.title: Speed
steps.detail: vx = 15 m/s, vy = -9.8 x 10 = -98 m/s, speed = sqrt(15 squared + 98 squared) approx 99 m/s.

spec.answer: Time 10 s; speed approx 99 m/s on hitting ground.

spec.problem: A cricket ball is thrown at 28 m s-1 in a direction 30 degrees above the horizontal. Calculate maximum height, time to return to same level, and distance to that point.

steps.title: Maximum height
steps.detail: hm = v0 squared sin squared 30 degrees / (2g) = 28 squared x 0.25 / (2 x 9.8) = 10.0 m.

steps.title: Time of flight
steps.detail: Tf = 2 v0 sin 30 degrees / g = 2 x 28 x 0.5 / 9.8 = 2.9 s.

steps.title: Range
steps.detail: R = v0 squared sin 60 degrees / g = 28 squared x sin 60 degrees / 9.8 approx 69 m.

spec.answer: Maximum height 10.0 m; time 2.9 s; distance 69 m.

spec.question: A cricketer can throw a ball to a maximum horizontal distance of 100 m. How high above the ground can the cricketer throw the same ball?
spec.explanation: Rmax = v0 squared / g = 100 m, so v0 squared = 100 g. Maximum height for same v0 is v0 squared / (2g) = 50 m. A ceiling limits height in the same way by limiting vertical component.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can relate maximum range and maximum height for same launch speed.

paragraphs: Uniform circular motion means following a circle at constant speed. Velocity direction changes continuously, so acceleration exists and points towards the centre.
Magnitude is ac equals v squared over R. Direction changes at every point, so acceleration is not a constant vector even though magnitude is constant.

spec.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 400 220'><circle cx='200' cy='110' r='80' fill='none' stroke='#1C1B18' stroke-width='2.6'/><circle cx='200' cy='110' r='4' fill='#1C1B18'/><line x1='200' y1='110' x2='260' y2='50' stroke='#1C1B18' stroke-width='2.6'/><line x1='260' y1='50' x2='320' y2='90' stroke='#1F3A9E' stroke-width='3'/><line x1='260' y1='50' x2='200' y2='110' stroke='#1F3A9E' stroke-width='3'/><polygon points='320,90 304,92 310,78' fill='#1F3A9E'/><polygon points='200,110 214,104 210,118' fill='#1F3A9E'/><text x='190' y='100' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>C</text><text x='265' y='45' fill='#1C1B18' font-size='20'>P</text><text x='325' y='85' fill='#1F3A9E' font-size='20'>v</text><text x='215' y='105' fill='#1F3A9E' font-size='20'>ac</text></svg>
spec.caption: Uniform circular motion: velocity v is tangent at P, acceleration ac is towards centre C. Circle radius is schematic.

steps.title: Angular speed
steps.detail: omega = delta theta / delta t, rate of change of angular displacement.

steps.title: Linear speed
steps.detail: Distance delta s = R delta theta, so v = delta s / delta t = R omega.

steps.title: Acceleration forms
steps.detail: ac = v squared / R = omega squared R. With period T and frequency n = 1/T, v = 2 pi R / T = 2 pi R n, omega = 2 pi n, ac = 4 pi squared n squared R.

spec.problem: An insect trapped in a circular groove of radius 12 cm moves steadily and completes 7 revolutions in 100 s. Find angular speed, linear speed, and magnitude of acceleration. Is acceleration a constant vector?

steps.title: Angular speed
steps.detail: omega = 2 pi x 7 / 100 = 0.44 rad/s.

steps.title: Linear speed
steps.detail: v = omega R = 0.44 x 12 cm = 5.3 cm/s, tangent to circle.

steps.title: Acceleration
steps.detail: a = omega squared R = 0.44 squared x 12 = 2.3 cm/s squared towards centre; direction changes, so not constant vector.

spec.answer: omega = 0.44 rad/s, v = 5.3 cm/s, a = 2.3 cm/s squared towards centre, not constant vector.

spec.question: A stone tied to a string 80 cm long is whirled in a horizontal circle with constant speed, making 14 revolutions in 25 s. What is magnitude and direction of acceleration?
spec.explanation: omega = 2 pi x 14 / 25 = 3.52 rad/s; ac = omega squared R = 12.4 x 0.80 approx 9.9 m/s squared, directed to centre.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can compute centripetal acceleration from revolutions and radius.

spec.question: An aircraft executes a horizontal loop of radius 1.00 km with steady speed 900 km/h. Compare its centripetal acceleration with g.
spec.explanation: 900 km/h = 250 m/s; ac = v squared / R = 250 squared / 1000 = 62.5 m/s squared; divided by 9.8 gives about 6.4 g.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can compare centripetal acceleration with g.

paragraphs: Path length depends on actual path; displacement depends only on end points. They are equal only if direction does not change. Average speed is therefore greater than or equal to magnitude of average velocity.

Vector equations for constant acceleration do not need a choice of axes, but you may resolve them along any two independent axes. Trajectory depends on initial position and velocity as well as acceleration. Resultant velocity is v1 plus v2, while relative velocity v12 is v1 minus v2 with respect to a common frame.

spec.question: Three girls start at P on a circular ground of radius 200 m and reach Q diametrically opposite by different paths. What is magnitude of displacement for each?
spec.explanation: Displacement is straight line PQ, the diameter 400 m, same for all. Path length equals displacement only for the girl who goes straight along the diameter.
spec.expected_understanding: Student distinguishes displacement from path length.

spec.question: A hotel is 10 km away on a straight road. A cab takes a 23 km circuitous path and reaches in 28 min. Find average speed and magnitude of average velocity.
spec.explanation: Average speed = 23 km / (28/60 h) approx 49 km/h. Magnitude of average velocity = 10 km / (28/60 h) approx 21 km/h. Path length differs from displacement, so they differ.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can compute average speed versus average velocity.

spec.question: What are magnitude and direction of i + j and i - j?
options: both sqrt(2), at 45 degrees and -45 degrees with x-axis
spec.explanation: i+j has components 1,1 magnitude sqrt(2) direction tan inverse 1 = 45 degrees. i-j has components 1,-1 magnitude sqrt(2) direction -45 degrees. Components along these directions can be found graphically by projection.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can find magnitude, direction and components of unit-vector combinations.

spec.question: Which statement about a scalar quantity is false?
options: it can never take negative values
it is specified by a number and a unit
it has the same value for observers with different axis orientations
spec.explanation: A scalar is defined by magnitude only; the source does not require it to be conserved, dimensionless, non-negative or constant in space. Temperature difference and other scalars show the definition is magnitude only.
spec.expected_understanding: Student does not over-generalise properties of scalars.

spec.question: Position is r = 3.0 t squared i - 2.0 t squared j + 4.0 t squared k metres, t in seconds. What is magnitude of velocity at t = 2.0 s?
spec.explanation: v = dr/dt = 6.0 t i - 4.0 t j + 8.0 t k; at 2.0 s v = 12 i - 8 j + 16 k, magnitude sqrt(144+64+256)=sqrt(464) approx 21.5 m/s. Acceleration is 6 i -4 j +8 k m/s squared.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can differentiate position to get velocity and acceleration.

spec.question: An aircraft flies at height 3400 m. Angle subtended at a ground point by positions 10.0 s apart is 30 degrees. Estimate speed, assuming the ground point is below the midpoint of the two positions.
spec.explanation: Half distance = 3400 x tan 15 degrees approx 911 m, total distance approx 1822 m in 10.0 s, speed approx 182 m/s. This uses the midpoint assumption stated because figure geometry is not fully readable in source.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can estimate speed from angle, height and time.
